To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of six fungicides at the recommended pre-harming interval does not affect the antioxidant activity of wines.
the antioxidant activity of wine is not affected by the presence of fungicide residues in grape at the pre-harmest interval and most unfavorable treatment conditions.
the use of the six fungicides did not affect the antioxidant activity of the wines obtained from grapes at the pre-harmvest interval and most unfavourable conditions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of the presence of fungicide residues on the phenolic content of the wine.
the influence of the presence of fungicide residues on the antioxidant capacity and the phenolic composition of red wine.
the evaluation of the influence of the use of several fungicides in the antioxidant activity and phenolic profile of the wines.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of the fungicides at the recommended dose, following GAP, did not produce any significant alteration in the antioxidant capacity of red wine.

the use of the six fungicides at the pre-harmful interval does not alter the antioxidant activity of the wine and, in some cases, the presence of these fungicide residues may even improve this activity.
the use of the six fungicides studied at the pre-h arvest interval and most critical conditions did not affect the antioxidant activity of the red wines obtained.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presence of the residues of the fungicides used in our study did not produce any deleterious effect on the wine phenolic compounds and antioxidant activity.

the use of the fungicides at the recommended pre-harmest interval and most favorable conditions did not affect the wine antioxidant activity and composition, but when the use of the same fungicides was carried out at the day of the harvest or under the most unfavorable conditions, the wine antioxidant activity increased and the wine composition changed.
the presence of the studied fungicides at the pre-harmest interval did not decrease the antioxidant activity and the phenolic composition of the wine.

the use of the fungicides at the pre-harpvest interval and most critical conditions does not affect the antioxidant capacity of the wines.
